subject: Food Science
title: Starter Cultures
description: Learn Starter Cultures in one minute.

hook.text: Every batch of Roquefort cheese uses the same Penicillium roqueforti strain—maintained since the 1800s.

buildup.text: Starter cultures are carefully selected microbe strains added to food to control fermentation predictably.

discovery.text: Without starters, wild microbes produce inconsistent results. Starters ensure every yogurt batch tastes the same.

twist.text: Sourdough uses wild starters—unique microbial communities from local flour and air. No two bakeries have the same mix.

climax.text: Culture banks preserve thousands of strains. Losing a starter culture would mean losing irreplaceable flavors.

punchline.text: Starter cultures are recipes made of living organisms. Guard them well.

quiz.question: Why are starter cultures used in food production?
options: To control fermentation and ensure consistent, predictable results
